ai_summary: Great Britain's total wind output currently stands at 4.2 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output delivering 1.8 GW, representing 17.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Driven by this regional generation, Scottish carbon intensity is at 0 gCO2/kWh, contrasting sharply with the 175 gCO2/kWh recorded GB-wide. Despite this abundance of zero-carbon power, cross-border transmission limits prevent electricity from flowing smoothly to southern demand centers. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 548 MWh, incurred at a constraint cost of about £27,101 through Balancing Mechanism bids. Because this renewable energy cannot be accommodated, fossil generation must ramp up to bridge the gap, resulting in an estimated 104,025 cubic meters of gas burned elsewhere to replace it, which released an additional 192 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Annualising today's run-rate indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £10 million. Across Great Britain's overall demand volume, this equates to an estimated increase of approximately £0.04/MWh on everybody's invoice in the UK, highlighting the compounding financial and environmental price of transmission network constraints.
